question: Which of the following statements is correct about the hydration enthalpies of alkali metals? \( \text{(a) Li}^+ \text{ has the highest hydration enthalpy} \) \( \text{(b) Na}^+ \text{ has higher hydration enthalpy than K}^+ \) \( \text{(c) Cs}^+ \text{ has the lowest hydration enthalpy} \) \( \text{(d) Hydration enthalpy decreases down the group} \)
explanation: The hydration enthalpy decreases down the group due to increasing ionic radius, making \( \text{Li}^+ \) the most hydrated.

question: Among the following, which alkali metal ion has the highest polarizing power? \( \text{(a) Na}^+ \) \( \text{(b) K}^+ \) \( \text{(c) Cs}^+ \) \( \text{(d) Li}^+ \)
explanation: Li\(^{+}\) has the smallest ionic radius and highest charge density, making its polarizing power highest.

question: Which of the following is a correct reaction of \( \text{H}_2 \text{O}_2 \) with sodium? \( \text{(a) 2Na + 2H}_2 \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2NaOH + \text{H}_2 \) \( \text{(b) 2Na + H}_2 \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2NaOH \) \( \text{(c) Na + H}_2 \text{O}_2 \rightarrow NaOH + \text{H}_2 \) \( \text{(d) Na + H}_2 \text{O}_2 \rightarrow {Na}_2 \text{O}_2 + \text{H}_2 \)
explanation: Sodium reacts with \( \text{H}_2 \text{O}_2 \) to form \( \text{NaOH} \) and \( \text{H}_2 \) gas as shown in option (a).

question: Identify the compound formed when lithium reacts with nitrogen. \( \text{(a) Li}_2 \text{N} \) \( \text{(b) LiN} \) \( \text{(c) Li}_3 \text{N} \) \( \text{(d) Li}_4 \text{N}_2 \)
explanation: Lithium forms \( \text{Li}_3\text{N} \) (lithium nitride) when reacting with nitrogen, which is stable due to lithium's small ionic size and high lattice energy.

question: Which of the following reactions represents the formation of NaH from Na? \( \text{(a) Na + H}_2 \rightarrow NaH \) \( \text{(b) 2Na + H}_2 \rightarrow 2NaH \) \( \text{(c) Na + H} \rightarrow NaH \) \( \text{(d) 2Na + H} \rightarrow 2NaH \)
explanation: Sodium hydride, \( \text{NaH} \), is formed by reacting sodium with hydrogen as shown in \( 2\text{Na} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NaH} \).

question: Which of the following alkali metals will have the highest first ionization energy? \( \text{(a) Li} \) \( \text{(b) Na} \) \( \text{(c) K} \) \( \text{(d) Cs} \)
explanation: Due to its small atomic size and strong nuclear attraction, lithium has the highest first ionization energy among alkali metals.

question: Which compound of sodium is used to extract titanium from titanium tetrachloride? \( \text{(a) NaOH} \) \( \text{(b) Na}_2 \text{O}_2 \) \( \text{(c) NaCl} \) \( \text{(d) NaH} \)
explanation: Sodium hydride (NaH) is used in the extraction of titanium as it reduces \( \text{TiCl}_4 \) to titanium.

question: Which hydrogen isotope is used in nuclear fusion reactions? \( \text{(a) Protium} \) \( \text{(b) Deuterium} \) \( \text{(c) Tritium} \) \( \text{d) Both b and c} \)
explanation: Both deuterium and tritium isotopes are used in nuclear fusion reactions due to their suitable nuclear properties.

question: Which of the following s-block metal hydroxides is amphoteric? \( \text{(a) NaOH} \) \( \text{(b) KOH} \) \( \text{(c) Mg(OH)}_2 \) \( \text{(d) Be(OH)}_2 \)
explanation: Beryllium hydroxide, \( \text{Be(OH)}_2 \), is amphoteric and can react with both acids and bases.

question: Which compound among the following has the highest lattice energy? \( \text{(a) NaCl} \) \( \text{(b) NaF} \) \( \text{(c) KCl} \) \( \text{(d) LiF} \)
explanation: LiF has the highest lattice energy due to the small ionic sizes of Li\(^{+}\) and F\(^{-}\) ions, resulting in a strong ionic bond.

question: Which of the following is the correct order of solubility of the hydroxides of alkali metals in water? \( \text{(a) LiOH < NaOH < KOH < CsOH} \) \( \text{(b) NaOH < KOH < LiOH < CsOH} \) \( \text{(c) CsOH < KOH < NaOH < LiOH} \) \( \text{(d) KOH < NaOH < LiOH < CsOH} \)
explanation: The solubility of alkali metal hydroxides increases down the group, so the correct order is \( \text{LiOH < NaOH < KOH < CsOH} \).

question: Among the following reactions, which correctly represents the reaction of \( \text{BeCl}_2 \) with water? \( \text{(a) BeCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Be(OH)}_2 + 2\text{HCl} \) \( \text{(b) BeCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{BeO} + 2\text{HCl} \) \( \text{(c) BeCl}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Be(OH)}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \) \( \text{(d) BeCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Be(OH)}_2 \text{ and } \text{HCl} \)
explanation: Beryllium chloride hydrolyzes in water to form \( \text{Be(OH)}_2 \) and \( \text{HCl} \), as shown in option (a).

question: Which of the following statements about alkali metals is incorrect? \( \text{(a) They have low ionization energies.} \) \( \text{(b) Their oxides are generally basic in nature.} \) \( \text{(c) They form stable complexes easily.} \) \( \text{(d) Their melting points decrease down the group.} \)
choice2: Their oxides are generally basic in nature.
choice4: Their melting points decrease down the group.
explanation: Alkali metals do not typically form stable complexes easily due to their large atomic size and low charge density.

question: Calculate the volume of \( \text{H}_2 \) gas produced at STP when 0.5 moles of \( \text{Na} \) reacts with excess water. \( \text{(a) 11.2 L} \) \( \text{(b) 5.6 L} \) \( \text{(c) 22.4 L} \) \( \text{(d) 16.8 L} \)
explanation: The reaction \( 2\text{Na} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2 \) produces 1 mole of \( \text{H}_2 \) for every 2 moles of \( \text{Na} \), so 0.5 moles of \( \text{Na} \) will produce 0.25 moles of \( \text{H}_2 \) gas, equivalent to 11.2 L at STP.

question: Which of the following hydrogen halides has the strongest hydrogen bond? \( \text{(a) HF} \) \( \text{(b) HCl} \) \( \text{(c) HBr} \) \( \text{(d) HI} \)
explanation: Hydrogen fluoride (HF) forms the strongest hydrogen bond due to the high electronegativity of fluorine and the small size of the \( \text{H–F} \) bond.

question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the inert pair effect? \( \text{(a) It is more prominent in lighter p-block elements.} \) \( \text{(b) It is due to the high bond dissociation energy of s-electrons.} \) \( \text{(c) It increases down the group in p-block elements.} \) \( \text{(d) It is due to poor shielding of d and f orbitals.} \)
choice1: It is more prominent in lighter p-block elements.
choice2: It is due to the high bond dissociation energy of s-electrons.
choice3: It increases down the group in p-block elements.
choice4: It is due to poor shielding of d and f orbitals.
explanation: The inert pair effect is more significant in heavier elements of p-block as it increases down the group due to the poor shielding by d and f orbitals.

question: In the structure of \( \text{XeF}_6 \), the geometry is distorted due to the presence of: \( \text{(a) lone pair-lone pair repulsions} \) \( \text{(b) lone pair-bond pair repulsions} \) \( \text{(c) bond pair-bond pair repulsions} \) \( \text{(d) none of these} \)
explanation: \( \text{XeF}_6 \) has a distorted octahedral geometry due to lone pair-bond pair repulsions as xenon has one lone pair.

question: Which of the following compounds has the highest thermal stability? \( \text{(a) CO}_2 \) \( \text{(b) SiO}_2 \) \( \text{(c) GeO}_2 \) \( \text{(d) SnO}_2 \)
explanation: SiO_2 has the highest thermal stability due to its strong \( \text{Si–O} \) bonds and network structure.

question: Which among the following oxides is acidic in nature? \( \text{(a) CO} \) \( \text{(b) SiO}_2 \) \( \text{(c) SnO} \) \( \text{(d) PbO} \)
explanation: SiO_2 is an acidic oxide as it reacts with bases to form silicates.

question: Which of the following halides of boron is the strongest Lewis acid? \( \text{(a) BF}_3 \) \( \text{(b) BCl}_3 \) \( \text{(c) BBr}_3 \) \( \text{(d) BI}_3 \)
explanation: BI_3 is the strongest Lewis acid due to the large size of iodine, which results in a weaker \( \text{B–I} \) bond and higher tendency to accept electrons.

question: The boiling point of \( \text{NH}_3 \) is higher than \( \text{PH}_3 \) due to: \( \text{(a) greater mass of NH}_3 \) \( \text{(b) greater dipole moment of PH}_3 \) \( \text{(c) hydrogen bonding in NH}_3 \) \( \text{(d) larger molecular size of NH}_3 \)
explanation: NH_3 has a higher boiling point than PH_3 because of hydrogen bonding present in \( \text{NH}_3 \).

question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about \( \text{SO}_3 \)? \( \text{(a) It forms anhydrides of sulfuric acid.} \) \( \text{(b) It has a planar structure.} \) \( \text{(c) It is a Lewis acid.} \) \( \text{(d) It has sp}^3 \text{ hybridization.} \)
choice1: It forms anhydrides of sulfuric acid.
explanation: SO_3 has \( \text{sp}^2 \) hybridization, resulting in a trigonal planar structure.

question: Which of the following is the correct stability order of oxidation states for Group 15 elements? \( \text{(a) +5 > +3 > -3} \) \( \text{(b) -3 > +3 > +5} \) \( \text{(c) +5 > +3 > +1} \) \( \text{(d) +3 > +5 > -3} \)
explanation: Group 15 elements exhibit a stability order of -3 > +3 > +5 for their oxidation states, especially evident with nitrogen.

question: Which of the following is not expected to react with \( \text{SO}_2 \) at room temperature? \( \text{(a) Cl}_2 \) \( \text{(b) O}_2 \) \( \text{(c) H}_2\text{O} \) \( \text{(d) I}_2 \)
explanation: I_2 is unreactive with \( \text{SO}_2 \) at room temperature due to the relatively low reactivity of iodine compared to \( \text{Cl}_2 \) and \( \text{O}_2 \).

question: Which of the following oxoacids of phosphorus contains a P-H bond? \( \text{(a) H}_3\text{PO}_3 \) \( \text{(b) H}_3\text{PO}_4 \) \( \text{(c) H}_3\text{P}_2\text{O}_5 \) \( \text{(d) H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7 \)
explanation: \( \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 \) (phosphorous acid) contains a \( \text{P-H} \) bond.

question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the stability of \( \text{ClO}_4^- \), \( \text{BrO}_4^- \), and \( \text{IO}_4^- \) ions? \( \text{(a) Stability decreases down the group} \) \( \text{(b) Stability increases down the group} \) \( \text{(c) All have equal stability} \) \( \text{(d) None of these} \)
explanation: The stability of \( \text{XO}_4^- \) ions increases down the group as the larger halide ions stabilize the \( \text{O}_4^- \) structure more effectively.

question: Which of the following halides is least likely to undergo hydrolysis? \( \text{(a) AlCl}_3 \) \( \text{(b) SiCl}_4 \) \( \text{(c) NCl}_3 \) \( \text{(d) PCl}_5 \)
explanation: \( \text{NCl}_3 \) is the least likely to hydrolyze because nitrogen does not have available d-orbitals to expand its octet and accept water molecules.

question: The thermal stability order of Group 16 hydrides is: \( \text{(a) H}_2\text{Te} > \text{H}_2\text{Se} > \text{H}_2\text{S} > \text{H}_2\text{O} \) \( \text{(b) H}_2\text{O} > \text{H}_2\text{S} > \text{H}_2\text{Se} > \text{H}_2\text{Te} \) \( \text{(c) H}_2\text{O} > \text{H}_2\text{Te} > \text{H}_2\text{Se} > \text{H}_2\text{S} \) \( \text{(d) H}_2\text{S} > \text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{H}_2\text{Se} > \text{H}_2\text{Te} \)
explanation: The stability of Group 16 hydrides decreases down the group as bond strength decreases from \( \text{H}_2\text{O} \) to \( \text{H}_2\text{Te} \).

question: Which of the following statements is true about \( \text{XeF}_2 \), \( \text{XeF}_4 \), and \( \text{XeF}_6 \)? \( \text{(a) All have square planar geometry} \) \( \text{(b) XeF}_4 is square planar while \text{XeF}_2 and \text{XeF}_6 are linear \) \( \text{(c) XeF}_2 is linear, \text{XeF}_4 is square planar, and \text{XeF}_6 has distorted octahedral geometry \) \( \text{(d) All have octahedral geometry} \)
choice2: \(XeF_4 \) is square planar while \(XeF_2 \) and \(XeF_6 \) are linear
choice3: \(XeF_2 \) is linear, \(XeF_4 \) is square planar, and \(XeF_6 \) has distorted octahedral geometry
explanation: \( \text{XeF}_2 \) is linear, \( \text{XeF}_4 \) is square planar, and \( \text{XeF}_6 \) has a distorted octahedral geometry due to the presence of lone pairs.

question: Which of the following has the highest bond angle? \( \text{(a) H}_2\text{O} \) \( \text{(b) NH}_3 \) \( \text{(c) CH}_4 \) \( \text{(d) Cl}_2\text{O} \)
explanation: \( \text{CH}_4 \) has the highest bond angle (109.5°) due to its tetrahedral structure.
